tasks.title: Hit ratio
tasks.statement: From the access log access_log(key, hit, ms): hit = 1 is a hit, 0 is a miss. Output the hit ratio as a percentage rounded to an integer (one column pct).
tasks.hint: SUM(hit) is the number of hits, COUNT(*) is the total; multiply by 100.0 to avoid integer division.

tasks.title: Hottest keys
tasks.statement: Output the three most frequent keys and the number of accesses for each (columns key, n); break ties by key.
tasks.hint: GROUP BY key, sort by count descending, LIMIT 3.

tasks.title: Average latency with and without cache
tasks.statement: Output the average latency (column ms) separately for hits and misses: columns hit, avg_ms (integer, rounded), ordered by hit.

tasks.title: Stale cache entries
tasks.statement: The cache table holds copies of rows from source. Output the ids of entries that must be invalidated: the version in the cache is lower than the version in the source, as well as entries that no longer exist in the source. Column id, ascending.
tasks.hint: LEFT JOIN cache → source: no match (IS NULL) or a lower version.

tasks.title: Refreshing the cache table
tasks.statement: Update cache from source with a single INSERT … SELECT … ON CONFLICT: insert new ids, and for existing ones update version and body, but only if the version in source is greater. The result is checked on the cache table.
tasks.hint: ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET … WHERE excluded.version > cache.version; WHERE true is needed so that SQLite can parse ON CONFLICT after SELECT.
tasks.starter:
-- sync cache from source
INSERT INTO cache

tasks.title: LRU cache: get and put
tasks.statement: A cache of capacity cap. Operations: ['put', key, value] and ['get', key]. put adds or updates (the entry becomes the freshest); on overflow the oldest is evicted. get returns the value and makes the entry the freshest. Write lru_run(cap, ops): a pair [list of get results (None on a miss), keys in the cache from the oldest to the freshest].
tasks.hint: An order list plus a dictionary of values; get and put move the key to the end of the list.

tasks.title: LFU: who to evict
tasks.statement: Access counters are a dictionary "key → count", the insertion order is the list keys (oldest to newest). The key with the fewest accesses is evicted; on a tie, the one inserted earlier. Write lfu_evict(keys, counts): the key to evict (None if the cache is empty).
tasks.hint: min over the pair (access count, position in the insertion list).

tasks.title: Cache with time to live
tasks.statement: Operations: ['put', t, key, value, ttl] and ['get', t, key]. An entry lives while t < t_put + ttl. Write ttl_run(ops): the list of get results (the value or None). A repeated put overwrites both the value and the expiry.
tasks.hint: Store the value and the expiry moment; get compares t with the expiry moment.

tasks.title: Cache-aside: how many trips to the database
tasks.statement: The requests are a list of keys to read. The cache is initially empty and unbounded. On a miss we read the database and put the value in the cache. Write cache_aside(reads): a pair [number of hits, number of database accesses].
tasks.hint: A set of keys in the cache: already there is a hit, otherwise a database access and add it.

tasks.title: Write-back
tasks.statement: The writes are a list of [key, value] in order. A write-back cache accumulates changes and flushes them to the database when batch distinct keys have accumulated, and flushes the remainder at the end. Write write_back_flush(writes, batch): the list of flushes, each a dictionary "key → latest value" at the moment of the flush (an empty list for no writes).
tasks.hint: A dictionary of "dirty" keys; when batch distinct keys are reached, add it to the result and start a new one.

tasks.title: How many requests reach the database
tasks.statement: At the moment an entry expires, n requests arrive at once. Without protection each goes to the database. With a single recompute (single-flight), one request goes to the database and the others wait. Write db_hits_on_expiry(n, single_flight): the number of database accesses (0 if there are no requests).
tasks.hint: Two cases: n or 1; zero requests means zero accesses.

tasks.title: TTL jitter
tasks.statement: So that entries do not expire in a bunch, a spread is added to the base period base. Deterministic version: for entry number i (from zero) the period = base + (i · step) % spread. Write ttl_with_jitter(base, spread, step, count): the list of periods for count entries (spread > 0).
tasks.hint: A list by the formula base + (i * step) % spread.

tasks.title: Negative caching
tasks.statement: The database is a dictionary "key → value"; a missing key gives None. The cache remembers both values and "not found" (the negative result). Database accesses are counted only on a cache miss. Write negative_cache(db, reads): a pair [list of answers, number of database accesses].
tasks.hint: The cache stores None too; check whether the key is present in the cache, not whether the value is truthy.

tasks.title: Cache key
tasks.statement: The key is built from the path and parameters: path + '?' + parameters "name=value" joined with '&', sorted by name. Empty parameters (value None) are skipped; with no parameters the '?' is not needed. Write cache_key(path, params): a string.
tasks.hint: Sort the pairs by name; format f"{k}={v}".

tasks.title: Key versions
tasks.statement: An entity's version is stored separately: a dictionary "entity → version". The cache key is "entity:version". Write versioned_keys(versions, bumps, entities): first apply bumps (a list of entities whose version grows by 1; a new entity goes from version 0 to 1), then return the list of keys for entities in the same order (an unknown entity has version 0).
tasks.hint: Copy the versions dictionary; increment in a loop; then build the keys.

tasks.title: Cache and database race
tasks.statement: Three events in time order: 'read_db' (the reader took v1 from the database), 'write' (the writer updated the database to v2 and deleted the cache entry), 'set_cache' (the reader put its version into the cache). Write stale_after(events): True if after all the events the cache holds a stale value, that is, 'set_cache' happened after 'write' and 'read_db' before 'write'.
tasks.hint: Staleness is only the order read_db < write < set_cache.

tasks.title: Expected latency
tasks.statement: Write expected_latency(hit, t_cache, t_db): hit·t_cache + (1 − hit)·t_db, rounded to two decimals; and a second value, how many times the database load dropped (1 / (1 − hit); return None when hit = 1). Return a pair.
tasks.hint: Two formulas; beware of division by zero when hit = 1.

tasks.title: Two-level cache
tasks.statement: L1 (in process) and L2 (shared) are unbounded sets of keys. Read: if the key is in L1, the answer is 'L1'; otherwise if it is in L2, the answer is 'L2' and the key goes into L1; otherwise 'DB', and the key goes into both L1 and L2. Write two_level(reads): the list of answers.
tasks.hint: Two sets; the order of checks is L1 → L2 → database.

tasks.title: Finding hot keys
tasks.statement: The access log is a list of keys. A key is hot if it accounts for at least share (a fraction from 0 to 1) of all accesses. Write hot_keys(log, share): the sorted list of hot keys.
tasks.hint: Count frequencies and compare c / n with share.
